key_insight: Parameter-specific sparsity lets a learned controller focus quantum gradient measurements on the qubit-wise commuting groups that matter most.
engineering_relevance: Relevance-guided measurement selection can reduce variational quantum algorithm shot costs while retaining energy accuracy close to full-group measurement.
method: Characterize sparse group contributions to parameter-shift gradients.
Predict group relevance from Hamiltonian, circuit, light-cone, and current-state features.
Select groups using a tunable coverage threshold, with exact contributions needed only for offline supervision.
evidence_signal: Across 15 molecular VQE settings, the method saved 49.6% of nominal gradient-measurement shots with a mean absolute energy gap of 5.67 mHa relative to Full-QWC.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the evaluated molecular settings remains unestablished, and nominal shot savings do not alone establish end-to-end runtime gains.
paper_title: Variational Relevance-Informed Sparsification of Term Measurements for Variational Quantum Algorithms
